questions.question: Tusu is a harvest festival celebrated in Jharkhand during the winter in the last day of _______ month.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Poush.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Tusu** is a **harvest festival **celebrated in **Jharkhand **during the** winter season.**
 
• It is celebrated on the **last day** of the **Poush month**, which usually falls in **January.**
 
• The festival is primarily celebrated by the **tribal communities **in Jharkhand.
 
• Tusu is a** symbol of gratitude** towards nature and its **bountiful resources.**
 
• During the festival, people dress up in** traditional attire**, perform **cultural dances** and **sing songs** in praise of nature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Phalguna **is the **twelfth month** of the Hindu calendar and falls between **February and March**. 

 
 
• It is the month of** Holi,** the festival of colors.
 
 
 
• **Chaitra** is the first month of the Hindu calendar and falls between **March and April.**
 
 
• It marks the** beginning of the new year** in many parts of India.
 
 
 
• **Magha** is the** eleventh month** of the Hindu calendar and falls between **January and February.**
 
 
• It is considered an auspicious month for performing **religious rituals.**
 
 
 
• **Poush** is the** tenth month **of the Hindu calendar and falls between **December and January**. 
 
 
• It is a month of **harvest festivals** celebrated in many parts of India.
 
 
 
• Hence, the correct answer is **option 4, Poush.**

questions.question: What is the meaning of reverse repo rate?

options.text: Rate at which RBI borrows money from foreign banks
Rate at which RBI borrows money from commercial banks
Rate at which commercial banks borrows money from RBI
Rate at which commercial banks borrows money from foreign banks

questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Rate at which RBI borrows money from commercial banks.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Reverse repo rate:**

 
 
• It is the** rate** at which the **Reserve Bank of India **(RBI) **borrows money** from **commercial banks.**
 
• It is a tool used by RBI to **control the money supply** in the economy.
 
• Repo rate is usually** higher **than the Reverse **repo rate**.
 
• A **higher reverse repo rate** means commercial banks will earn **higher returns **by lending to RBI, leading to a **decrease in lending** to customers and a **decrease in money supply** in the economy.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1** is **incorrect **as RBI does not borrow from foreign banks, it only **lends** to them.
 
• **Option 3** is the **repo rate**, not the reverse repo rate.
 
• **Option 4 **is **incorrect **as commercial banks borrow from RBI, not foreign banks.
 
• Reverse repo rate is an important tool in **monetary policy** as it helps RBI control **inflation **and maintain **economic stability.**

questions.question: Jyotiba Phule founded the Satyashodhak Samaj (Truth Seekers’ Society) in ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1873.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jyotiba Phule **founded the** Satyashodhak Samaj** in **1873.**
 
• Satyashodhak Samaj was founded with the aim of **liberating the lower castes** from the **oppression **of the **upper castes** in Hindu society.
 
• Jyotiba Phule was a **social reformer **who played a crucial role in the **upliftment** of the** lower castes and women **in **Maharashtra.**
 
• He also founded the **first school for girls** in **Pune in 1848** and was a strong advocate for **women's education.**
 
• **Option 1** (1852) and **Option 4** (1865) are** incorrect **as Jyotiba Phule founded Satyashodhak Samaj in 1873.
 
• **Option 3** (1898) is also** incorrect **as Jyotiba Phule passed away in **1890.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jyotiba Phule** was born in **1827** in **Maharashtra, India** and belonged to a **lower caste.**
 
• He was a strong critic of the **caste system **and **Brahminical patriarchy **in Hindu society.
 
• **Option 1 **(1852) is close to the actual year of **Jyotiba Phule's first social work**, where he opened a **school for the untouchables **in Pune, but it is not the year he founded Satyashodhak Samaj.
 
• **Option 4 **(1865) is also close to the year when Jyotiba Phule started the** Satyashodhak movement,** but it is not the year when he founded Satyashodhak Samaj.
 
• Hence, the **correct answer** is **option 2 (1873).**

questions.question: Which device is used for measuring temperature?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Thermometer.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A** thermometer** is a device used for **measuring temperature.**
 
• It works on the principle of** thermal expansion**, which means that the material used in the **thermometer expands or contracts** depending on the **temperature.**
 
• The most common type of thermometer is a **mercury thermometer**, which consists of a **glass tube **filled with **mercury.**
 
 
• As the **temperature rises**, the mercury** expands and rises** in the tube, indicating the **temperature.**
 
 
 
• Other types of thermometers include **digital thermometers, infrared thermometers, and bimetallic thermometers**.
 
• Hence, the** correct option** is 3) Thermometer.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Manometer** is a device used for measuring **pressure.**
 
• **Ammeter **is used for measuring **electrical current.**
 
• **Barometer** is used for measuring **atmospheric pressure.**

questions.question: Who among the following Gupta kings founded the Nalanda University?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kumaragupta I.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Chandragupta II, also known as **Vikramaditya,** was a famous **Gupta king** who ruled from** 375 to 415 CE**.

 
 
• He was known for his **military conquests** and **patronage of the arts,** but there is no evidence that he founded Nalanda University.
 
 
 
• Chandragupta I was the** founder of the Gupta dynasty** and ruled from **320 to 335 CE**.
 
 
• He was known for his **military campaigns** and **administrative reforms**, but he lived before the establishment of Nalanda University.
 
 
 
• Kumaragupta I was a Gupta king who ruled from **415 to 455 CE.**
 
 
• He was a patron of the** arts and literature.**
 
• He is credited with founding **Nalanda University.**
 
 
 
• Skandagupta was a **Gupta king** who ruled from **455 to 467 CE**.
 
 
• He was known for his **military campaigns** against the Huns, but there is no evidence that he founded Nalanda University.
 
 
 
• Hence, the correct answer is **Option 3 (Kumaragupta I).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nalanda University** was founded in the **5th century CE **in present-day **Bihar, India.**
 
• It was one of the **oldest and most prestigious centers **of learning in ancient India, attracting **students and scholars** from all over the world.
 
• The university was supported by **various Gupta kings,** who were known for their patronage of** art, literature, and education.**

questions.question: Which is the first garden - tomb in the Indian subcontinent?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Humayun's Tomb.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Humayun's Tomb** is located in **Delhi** and was built in the **mid-16th century.**
 
• It was commissioned by Humayun's widow, **Haji Begum**, and was designed by** Persian architect Mirak Mirza Ghiyas.**
 
• The tomb is a fine example of** Mughal architecture **and is considered to be the **first garden-tomb **in the Indian subcontinent.
 
• It has been declared a** UNESCO World Heritage Site **and is a popular tourist attraction in **Delhi**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Taj Mahal:** This is a **mausoleum** located in** Agra.**

 
 
• It was** **built by **Mughal emperor Shah Jahan** for his wife **Mumtaz Mahal**.
 
• While it is a beautiful example of Mughal architecture, it is not a garden-tomb.
 
 
 
• **Qutb Shahi Tombs:** These are a group of tombs located in **Hyderabad.**
 
 
• These were** **built by the **Qutb Shahi dynasty.**
 
• While they are impressive examples of **Islamic architecture, **they are not the first garden-tombs in the Indian subcontinent.
 
 
 
• **Aurangzeb's Tomb:** This is located in** Khuldabad, Maharashtra.**
 
 
• **It **was built for **Mughal emperor Aurangzeb.**
 
• However, it is not considered to be a garden-tomb and is** not as well-known** as the other options.

questions.question: Most of the Himalayan rivers are of which type?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Perennial.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Most of the Himalayan rivers are **perennial**, meaning they** flow throughout the year.**
 
• In India **Himalayan Rivers **like **Ganga and Bhramaputra** are **perennial rivers.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Exotic rivers **are those tha**t originate outside** a region and** flow into it.**
 
• In the case of the **Himalayas,** this would refer to rivers like the** Indus and Brahmaputra.**
 
• **Seasonal rivers** flow only during** certain seasons**, usually during **monsoon season **when there is **heavy rainfall.**
 
• **Episodic rivers** are those that flow only during** rare events,** such as **flash floods or heavy rainstorms.**
 
• Therefore, the **correct answer **to the question is** option 2, perennial.**

questions.question: The third battle of Panipat fought in ________.

• This battle was fought between the **Maratha Empire **and the** Durrani Empire.**
 
• The Marathas were led by **Sadashivrao Bhau**, while the **Durrani Empire **was led by **Ahmad Shah Durrani.**
 
• The battle was one of the **largest and bloodiest** fought in the **18th century,** with an estimated **60,000 to 70,000 casualties.**
 
• The **Durrani Empire** emerged **victorious** in the battle, which had a significant impact on the **political and military landscape **of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The year **1556** is associated with the** Battle of Panipat.**

 
 
• It was fought between the **Mughal Empire** and the** forces of Hemu,** the Prime Minister of the** Kingdom of Delhi.**
 
• The **Mughals **emerged victorious in this battle.
 
 
 
• The year 1651 is **not associated **with any significant battle in the history of India.
 
• The year **1526** is associated with the **First Battle of Panipat.**
 
 
• It** **was fought between the **Mughal Empire** and the forces of **Ibrahim Lodi, the Sultan of Delhi.**
 
• The **Mughals **emerged victorious in this battle.
 
 
 
• The year **1761** is associated with the **Third Battle of Panipat**, as discussed above.

questions.question: If we sum the gross value added of all the firms of the economy in a year, we get a measure of the value of aggregate amount of goods and services produced by the economy in a year. Such an estimate is called ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Gross domestic product.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gross Domestic Product (GDP)** is a measure of the **total value of all goods and services** produced within a country's borders in a **specific period, usually a year.**
 
• It is calculated by** summing up** the value of all** final goods and services **produced in the economy, including **consumption, investment, government spending, and net exports.**
 
• GDP is an important indicator of the** health of an economy**, as it reflects the **level of economic activity.**
 
• **GDP** can be used to compare the performance of **different countries or regions.**
 
• **National Income at Factor Cost (NIFC) **is the total income earned by **all factors of production **in an economy, including** wages, salaries, rent, interest, and profits.**
 
• **Net Value Added (NVA)** is the value of output produced by a firm after** deducting the cost of intermediate inputs**, such as** raw materials and energy.**
 
• **Net National Product (NNP) **is the total value of all goods and services produced by the** citizens of a country**, including those** produced abroad, minus the depreciation of capital goods.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **National Income at Factor Cost (NIFC)** is calculated by **deducting indirect taxes **and **adding subsidies** from GDP.
 
• **Net Value Added (NVA)** is a measure of the contribution made by a firm to the economy, and it is calculated by **subtracting **the value of **intermediate inputs** from the **total value of output.**
 
• **Net National Product (NNP)** is calculated by deducting** depreciation from Gross National Product (GNP),** which is the total value of all goods and services produced by the** citizens of a country,** including those produced abroad. 
 
• In the given question, Gross Domestic Product (GDP) is the **correct answer** as it is a measure of the total value of** all goods and services** produced within a country's borders in a specific period.

questions.question: Which of the following programme was launched in 1999?

options.text: Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee scheme

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (SGSY) **was launched in **1999.**
 
• It was launched by the** Ministry of Rural Development** to provide **self-employment **opportunities to **rural poor.**
 
• SGSY aimed to bring the **assisted poor families (Swarozgaris)** above the **poverty line** by organizing them into **Self Help Groups (SHGs) **through a mix of **bank credit and government subsidy.**
 
• The scheme was implemented in both** rural and urban areas.**
 
• **It **covered all aspects of** self-employment,** including **agriculture, horticulture, animal husbandry, fisheries,** and non-farm activities like **handicrafts, handlooms, and khadi.**
 
• SGSY was later renamed as **National Rural Livelihood Mission (NRLM)** in **2011.**
 
• **It i**s currently being implemented across the country to alleviate **poverty** and promote **sustainable livelihoods.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rural Employment Generation Programme (REGP)** was launched in **1995.**

 
 
• It aimed to create **sustainable self-employment opportunities **in rural areas through the **establishment of micro-enterprises.**
 
 
 
• **Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee scheme (MGNREGA)** was launched in **2005.**
 
 
• Its goal was to provide at least **100 days of guaranteed wage employment** to every** rural household** whose adult members volunteer to do **unskilled manual work.**
 
 
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Gramodaya Yojana (PMGY) **was launched in **2000.**
 
 
• ​Its goal was to provide basic amenities like **drinking water, primary healthcare,** and **primary education to rural areas.**

questions.question: Pandit Birju Maharaj was honoured with Padma Vibhushan award for which form of classical dance?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kathak.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pandit Birju Maharaj** was honoured with **Padma Vibhushan** award for **Kathak.**
 
• Kathak is a form of** classical dance **that originated in **North India.**
 
• Kathak is known for its** intricate footwork, fast spins**, and **storytelling **through **mime and gesture.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Manipuri **is a classical dance form from Manipur.

 
 
• It is known for its **graceful movements, lyrical quality**, and use of **traditional costumes and props**.
 
 
 
• **Jhumar **is a** folk dance** form from **Punjab.**
 
 
• It is traditionally performed by** men** and involves **vigorous movements and acrobatics.**
 
 
 
• **Mohiniattam **is a classical dance form from **Kerala**.
 
• It is known for its** fluid movements, delicate hand gestures,** and **facial expressions.**
 
• Hence, the **correct answer** is option 2.

questions.question: Which of the following book is the autobiography of Milkha Singh?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The Race of My Life.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Milkha Singh** is a former Indian track and field sprinter who is also known as **"The Flying Sikh".**
 
• Milkha Singh's autobiography, **The Race of My Life: An Autobiography, **was cowritten with her daughter **Sonia Sanwalka. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **"Touch Play"** is a book written by **Anand Pillai **which is about the **game of cricket.**
 
• **"Two Lives"** is a book written by **Vikram Seth** which is a memoir about his **family history.**
 
• **"Romancing My Life"** is a book written by **Dev Anand **which is his autobiography.
 
• Hence, the statement "The correct answer is **option 4"** is correct.

questions.question: Kathakali took shape in Southern India in the seventeenth century under the patronage of the ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Prince of Karnataka.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Kathakali** is a** classical dance-drama** form that originated in the state of** Kerala** in** Southern India** in the **seventeenth century.**
 
• It was developed under the** patronage** of the **Prince of Karnataka**, who was a **great patron **of the **arts and literature.**
 
• The Prince of Karnataka was a great admirer of the** traditional dance and theatre** forms of Kerala.
 
• He encouraged the artists to develop a new form o**f dance-drama **that would be more** vibrant and expressive.**
 
• The artists of Kerala, under the guidance of the Prince of Karnataka, developed** Kathakali**, which combines elements of **dance, music, drama, and ritual.**
 
• **Option 3**, Prince of Karnataka, is the **correct answer** as he was the patron of the art form.

questions.question: Under which type of unemployment a person contributes less than their capability?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Disguised unemployment.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Disguised unemployment** is a situation where a person appears to be** employed and working,** but their **contribution **to the economy is** less than their capability.**
 
• This type of unemployment often occurs in **agricultural or informal sectors** where there are **too many workers** for the available work, leading to **underemployment.**
 
• Hence, the **correct answer **is option 2, disguised unemployment, where a person contributes less than their capability.​

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Frictional unemployment **refers to the** temporary **unemployment that occurs when a person is in** between jobs or searching for a job.**
 
• **Compulsory unemployment** is a situation where the government or an employer **forces a person to be unemployed**, such as during a **strike **or due to **discrimination.**
 
• **Cyclical unemployment** is a type of unemployment that occurs due to **fluctuations in the business cycle**, where economic downturns lead to **job losses.**

questions.question: The First Field Handball World Championships were played in Germany in ________.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**1938.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The** first Field Handball World Championships** were held in** Berlin, Germany,** from 3-11 **September 1938.**
 
• The tournament featured** eight teams,** including Germany, Denmark, Sweden, Czechoslovakia, Switzerland, Hungary, Austria, and Italy.
 
• **Germany** won the inaugural championship, **defeating Denmark **10-6 in the final.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **For women, the first field handball World Championship** was held in **1949 in Hungary**.
 
• Six teams took part - **Hungary, Austria, Yugoslavia, Romania, Sweden, and Denmark**.
 
• The host nation, Hungary, won the tournament. 
 
• However, the game has primarily been played indoors since then, and modern handball (also called team handball or European handball) is what most people think of when talking about the sport today.
 
• Indoor handball is also the version that is included in the Summer Olympics.

questions.question: Which country is the biggest producer of rice?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**China.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **China** is the **biggest producer** of rice in the world, producing around **146 million metric tons** of rice in **2019.**
 
• **Rice** is a **staple food** in China and is consumed by a large population.
 
• It is also** exported** to other countries.
 
• **Russia **is **not **a major producer of rice as it has a **cold climate **and rice cultivation is **not feasible **there.
 
• **Brazil **is a major producer of crops like **soybean, corn, and coffee**, but it is not a major producer of rice.
 
• **Bangladesh** is a significant producer of rice, but its production is **much lower** than China.
 
• Bangladesh produced around **35 million metric tons **of rice in **2019.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rice** is the **staple food** for more than **half of the world's population.**
 
• Other major rice-producing countries include** India, Indonesia, Vietnam, and Thailand.**
 
• **Russia** is a major producer of **wheat, barley,** and other grains.
 
• **Brazil** is the largest producer of** coffee **in the world and is also a major producer of **soybeans, corn, and sugar.**
 
• **Bangladesh** is a densely populated country and** rice** is the **staple food **there.
 
• Hence, the statement "The correct answer is** option 2 (China)"** is correct.
